newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on wary attitude.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on wary attitude.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Tuesday with most investors cautious about the market trend in the short term, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 23,600 yuan ($2,845) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at 23,850 and hit a high of 23,860.
March fell 100 to 23,150, April rose 40 to 23,480, May fell 30 to 23,560, July was down 10 to 23,580 and August fell 150 to 23,550.
Combined volume rose to 47,800 tonnes from 32,840.
Copper opened higher due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, but profit-taking pushed most contracts down to close at or near their intra-day lows.
Traders said most investors took a wait-and-see attitude on concerns about a possible correction in the short term after sharp gains in the past two weeks.
"The expectation of a correction discouraged long position holders, resulting in the day's liquidation," one trader said.
"Many investors stayed on the sidelines with the short-term market trend unclear," he added.
Traders said most investors had accumulated heavy profits during the past two weeks and their wish to take profits was very strong.
"Taking profits and awaiting fresh market-moving news seems now a good idea," a second trader said.
Analysts expected copper to consolidate in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up. March rose 150 yuan to 16,150 yuan per tonne, April 100 to 16,450, May 80 to 16,780 and June 80 to 16,980. Combined volume fell to 4,700 tonnes from 5,380.
